headline: Big Ten Championship Game scenarios: Breaking down the four-team race with UCLA, Oregon, Indiana, Iowa alive
author: Brad Crawford

paragraphs.text: Nov 28, 2026 at 3:46 pm ET • 3 min read
So much for Ohio State and USC rooting for Nebraska to upset 13th-ranked Iowa on Friday.
There's no chaotic Big Ten Championship scenario unfolding now after the Hawkeyes' suffocating 31-7 win pushed them closer to Indianapolis next weekend.

Quarterback Hank Brown's 6-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter against Nebraska pushed Iowa's lead to 10 points, more than enough for one of the nation's best defenses to carry the Hawkeyes the rest of the way.

Now, Iowa awaits the rest of Rivalry Week's results to see if they've done enough to make next week's Big Ten Championship Game in Indianapolis. That brings the conference down to four teams battling for two spots -- the Hawkeyes, No. 9 UCLA, 12th-ranked Oregon and No. 14 Indiana.

Iowa finishes 7-2 in conference play this season, while the Hoosiers and Ducks will try to follow suit on Saturday. All the Hawkeyes need now -- in the most simplistic scenario -- is a loss from Oregon against Washington or losses from Indiana and current league-leading UCLA to Purdue and USC, respectively.
Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz is seeking his fourth career trip to the league title game.

"I just told the guys, winning 10 games is really an accomplishment, tough to do in college football any year," Ferentz said after the game. "I think I feel really good about that, and I've encouraged them to feel good about it. We've got a little time, whether it's Sunday or next Tuesday before we get started again. I just want them to really take a day and a half to really enjoy it. You don't get to do that very often in this racket, so I think it's really important that they do that, and they should."
Wisconsin's win over Minnesota on Friday night also lessened the chances Indiana will make it to Indianapolis. The Hoosiers' only path now is to beat Purdue and hope for losses by Oregon and UCLA.
Big Ten Championship Game clinch scenarios
Indiana
• Indiana win AND Oregon and UCLA losses
Iowa
• Indiana and Oregon losses OR
• Oregon win AND Indiana and UCLA losses OR
• Indiana, Oregon wins AND UCLA loss OR
• Indiana and UCLA wins, Oregon loss
Oregon
• Oregon win AND UCLA win OR
• Oregon win AND Indiana win AND UCLA loss
UCLA
• UCLA win OR
• UCLA loss AND Indiana and Oregon losses OR
• UCLA loss AND Oregon win AND Indiana loss OR
• UCLA loss AND Indiana and Ohio State wins AND Oregon loss OR
Ohio State's long-shot title game hopes hinged on a victory over Michigan, wins from Maryland, Rutgers and Wisconsin, and losses from Indiana, Iowa, Oregon and USC to get there.

Beginning with an Iowa loss to Nebraska, USC's various paths were more direct. However, now Lincoln Riley's team will try to topple 10-win UCLA, spoil the Bruins' CFP placement and keep their rival out of the Big Ten Championship.
Big Ten's faint multi-team CFP path

The winner of the Big Ten is going to the 12-team playoff -- that much, we know. However, there's a chance the Big Ten could produce only one representative this season based on the CFP selection committee's fourth rankings -- and only one team (No. 9 UCLA) inside the top 12.

If the Bruins beat USC, they're in next week's Big Ten Championship with 11 wins, which might be enough to warrant at-large inclusion even if Bob Chesney's team loses the conference title. But if the Trojans win, that would put Oregon and Indiana in the championship game, with only the winner earning an automatic bid to the bracket.

Entering Rivalry Week, UCLA was the only Big Ten team in control of its destiny. CFP chair Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday night that UCLA's five-spot drop in the latest rankings "did not have anything to do" with starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach's injury.
Dieffenbach suffered a hip bruise at Michigan and will start for the Bruins against the Trojans.
